clue.text: Muscle energy and power needed in last half of aerobics

indicators.note: needed in says the two abbreviations are placed inside the other letters
last half of takes the final four of the eight letters of aerobics

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A fitness tip: the arm muscles need energy and power in the second half of an aerobics class.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper-arm flexor is the best-known example of a muscle.

clue.text: Bring up book on freshwater fish

parts.note: the roach is a European freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Mention a book about a river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it for discussion.

clue.text: Keeping in mind company millions — note and share

parts.note: M stands for million
a memo is a short note
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A business making millions sends a memo about dividends.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of remembering or honouring something is a way of holding it in memory.

clue.text: Range of colourings allowed in meat paste

indicators.note: in places the word for allowed inside the meat paste

parts.note: pate is a spread of meat paste
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Food colourings are permitted in meat spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's selection of colours, or the board holding them, is the range on offer.

clue.text: Site of impact of old plane beside river

parts.note: crate is slang for an old, rickety aeroplane

explanation.surface: An aircraft wreck lies beside a river where it came down.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl-shaped hole is what a meteor or shell leaves at the point where it struck.

clue.text: Step right up for review

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters read upward, so backwards

parts.note: a pace is a step

explanation.surface: An instruction to come forward for an assessment.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary going over the main points again is a review of them.

clue.text: Ring in Rheingold set unconventionally as an operetta

indicators.note: in places the ring shape inside the rearranged letters
unconventionally means the letters of Rheingold set are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring, staged unconventionally, becomes a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Das Rheingold is the first opera of Wagner's Ring cycle, so 'Ring' looks like a reference to it, but it just gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, the classic English operetta form.

clue.text: Weapon of Royal Artillery atop bridge support

indicators.note: atop in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge span

explanation.surface: An artillery weapon positioned on top of a bridge pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, slender sword is a weapon used for thrusting.

clue.text: How Mal's broken rule in physics

indicators.note: broken tells us the letters of How Mal's are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how someone called Mal managed to break a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The law relating voltage, current and resistance is a basic principle of electrical physics.

clue.text: Little resistance about strict character from the free world

indicators.note: about says the small word goes around the strict word

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
stern describes a strict character
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A little opposition to a strict figure from the West.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cold War terms the free world was the West, so someone from it is a Westerner.

clue.text: Inexpensive hat that man's wearing

indicators.note: wearing means the hat goes around the man, so his letters sit inside

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
that man is, i.e. HE, the pronoun for a male

explanation.surface: A cheap hat is what that fellow has on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms for low in price.

clue.text: Conservative opponents of right in split

parts.note: the political left opposes the right

explanation.surface: Tories and their left-wing opponents are divided.
explanation.definitionFit: A split or fissure is a synonym, as in a cleft in rock.

clue.text: Assume drink leads to attitude

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a pose is an attitude or affected stance

explanation.surface: Presume that drinking produces a certain attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume something is to take it as given without proof; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Old writer finished, with more that might be written

definitions.text: with more that might be written

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
ended means finished

explanation.surface: An old author has finished, though more might yet have been written.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlimited or unconcluded can be extended further, leaving room for more to be added.

clue.text: Let down plane into Chester's river

indicators.note: into puts the plane inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Dee flows through Chester, a city in north-west England
a plane is a flat surface

explanation.surface: An aircraft crashes into the river at Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: To let down a tyre or balloon is to release its air.

clue.text: Wearing shoes dirty on the outside and badly made

parts.note: shod means wearing shoes

indicators.note: on the outside takes only the end letters of dirty

explanation.surface: Footwear muddy on the outside and poorly made.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy goods are cheap and of poor quality.

clue.text: British taken in and defeated

parts.note: eaten means taken in as food

explanation.surface: A Briton is deceived and beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms for overcome in a contest.

clue.text: Like savages cook chicken

parts.note: to heat food is to cook it
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: Savages are imagined cooking a chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes the uncivilised or unenlightened, which is the old notion of savages.

clue.text: Husky sounded to be a working animal

indicators.note: sounded says to take the spoken form of the first word

parts.note: a husky voice is a hoarse one

explanation.surface: A sled dog sounded like a beast of burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like the sled dog, which would be a working animal itself, but here it describes a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught or plough animal is the classic example of an animal used for work.

clue.text: Some tales La Fontaine rejected could be untrue

indicators.note: rejected means the letters are thrown back, read in the opposite direction
Some means only part of the words tales La Fontaine is taken

explanation.surface: Some of La Fontaine's fables, rejected, might not be true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ESLAF from 'talES LA Fontaine', and 'rejected' turns it round. Jean de La Fontaine was a French writer of fables.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are straightforward synonyms meaning not correct.

clue.text: Motorist drops velocity with less rain?

indicators.note: drops says one letter is taken out of the motorist

parts.note: a driver is a motorist
V is the physics symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A driver slows down when the weather improves.
explanation.definitionFit: A drier spell of weather is one with less rainfall; the question mark marks the playful definition.

clue.text: Chemical for testing is concerning a good man

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
a gent is a gentleman, a good man

explanation.surface: A lab sample about a decent fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used to detect or test for another in chemical analysis is a reagent.

clue.text: Roy and Den dancing together over there

indicators.note: dancing together means the letters of both names move around and mix

explanation.surface: Two men, Roy and Den, are dancing over at the far side.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old-fashioned word for at that distant place.

clue.text: Admiral in the hold for fighting?

definitions.meaning: Horatio, the British admiral who won at Trafalgar
a wrestling hold applied from behind, under the arms and behind the neck

explanation.surface: An admiral grips something in a ship's hold ready for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral is the Trafalgar hero; the full and half versions are standard wrestling holds.
